result.topic_en: Euler adds to the elastic forces the external forces needed to hold the column in its assumed bent state: horizontal forces A and B at the ends, the vertical reaction 2M at the base, and the weight acting at the centre of gravity G. He then begins the equilibrium conditions, starting with A + B = C for the horizontal forces.

lor autem nondum eſt cognitus, quandoquidem praeciſe

Deinde quia terminus inferior B fundo ita inſiſtere aſſu-
mitur, vt etiam de ſuo loco dimoueri nequeat, primo
ipſum fundum ſuſtinebit totum columnae pondus, vnde
ipſum punctum B ſurſum vrgeri cenſendum eſt vi $BO =$
$2M$; dein vero, ne de ſuo loco, ſiue dextrorſum ſiue ſini-
ſtrorſum, dimoueatur, illi vim horizontalem $Bb = B$ ap-
plicatam concipiamus, quae etiam inter incognita eſt refe-
renda. Tota autem columna ſuo pondere ita aget, quaſi
eius pondus in communi centro grauitatis G vtriusque
brachii eſſet applicatum, quod quia in medium interualli
CO cadit, erit $OG = \frac{1}{2} a\theta$, cuius ergo directio erit recta
verticalis $Gg$.
